payload.rationale: Observed facts: the FOMC hiked 25bp on Sept 16, 2026 to 3.75–4.00% (midpoint 3.875%) unanimously, citing solid growth and elevated inflation. The September SEP median end-2026 midpoint is 4.1% (range 3.9–4.4%), which implies exactly one more 25bp hike across the two remaining meetings (October and December 9); some participants see no further hikes, a few see two. Inflation remains well above target (Aug CPI 3.4% y/y, core PCE projected 3.4%), unemployment is 4.1%, and payrolls rebounded in August after weak June/July prints. Scenario weighting: (a) hike in October then hold in December ~30%; (b) hold in October, hike in December ~30%; (c) hold at both ~22%; (d) hike at both ~15%; (e) cut or other ~3%. YES (hold in December) = (a)+(c) ≈ 52–55%, nudged slightly up by the Fed's general tendency to hold at most meetings and by the rule that a canceled meeting resolves 'maintain' to Yes. Too high risk: the committee has momentum, inflation is sticky, and hikers may prefer to act at both remaining meetings or wait for December's SEP meeting to deliver the projected hike, making a December move more likely than a hold. Too low risk: policy is already at or above the low end of the projected range; weak mid-year payrolls and any growth slowdown could persuade the committee to stop after one more hike in October or pause entirely, and the Fed often front-loads then waits to assess, which favors a December hold.
limitations: Year-end projection does not specify which meeting delivers the additional hike; October versus December timing is the key uncertainty.
No meeting-specific data beyond September; upcoming CPI, PCE, and jobs releases (starting Oct 2) could shift the outlook materially.
Small evidence packet with no fitted model; scenario weights are judgmental.
Shocks (financial stress, energy prices, fiscal or political events) could produce cuts or larger moves not captured here.
